expectations.name: whole-frontend-on-the-fixture
expected_behavior: Opens with one line naming the frontend root (`web/`), the target, the files in scope, and the line width with its source

Reports the project `biome.json` as missing the reference settings — the HTML formatter and the rules the reference turns on beyond `recommended`, such as `useNamingConvention`, `noFloatingPromises`, and `useVueDefineMacrosOrder` — graded Blocker
Reports the unchecked `as { data: Site[] }` cast in `sites()` in `src/api.ts` as a Blocker
Reports the string-path link `` :to="`/?site=${s.id}`" `` in `src/pages/SitesPage.vue`
Reports the TSDoc starting with the symbol's name (`formatDate returns …`) in `src/format.ts`
Reports `toBeTruthy()` in `src/pages/SitesPage.test.ts`
Reports the `px` sizes (`gap: 24px`, `padding: 12px 24px`) in `src/components/AppLayout.vue`, and not the `1px` border
Reports the `qry` abbreviation in `src/pages/DevicesPage.vue`
Flags nothing in `src/read.ts`, `src/router.ts`, `src/stores/`, `src/components/DeviceTable.vue`, `src/components/LoadError.vue`, or `e2e/app.spec.ts`

Re-reports none of the rules the reference Biome config enforces as code offenses: no offense cites a `noNonNullAssertion`, `useImportType`, `noFloatingPromises`, or naming-convention case in the code
Each offense carries `file:line`, a derived rule id, the quoted trigger, and a fix opening with insert, delete, rename, move, replace, or reword
Asks which offenses to apply before editing anything, and after the answer `none` leaves every fixture file unchanged

expectations.name: fix-one-file-behind-a-green-gate
expected_behavior: Runs `bun run check` in `web/` for a green baseline before editing
Replaces the `px` gap and padding in `src/components/AppLayout.vue` with `rem` values and leaves the `1px` border
Re-runs `bun run check` after the edit and reports it green
Reports each fix as one `file:symbol — what changed` line plus the gate result, prints no diff, and never commits

expectations.name: reference-while-writing-a-page
expected_behavior: The new page's script puts its component TSDoc after the imports, above the first statement
The page reads through `useRead` (no hand-rolled `busy`/`error` refs) and starts the read with `onMounted(() => void …)`
Navigation to it and from it uses named routes, and the route is named in kebab-case and lazy-loaded
Its test fakes `fetch` through `fakeFetch` with `"GET /path"` keys and mounts with `mountAt`, inside one `describe("ModelsPage")`
